```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 9.0
#| fig-height: 3.4
#| out-width: "800px"
#| out-height: "280px"

library(grid)

draw_person <- function(x, y, s = 0.05, 
                        torso_col = "#334155", 
                        head_col = "#FDE68A", 
                        collar_col = "#FFFFFF",
                        tie_col = NULL) {
  head_r <- s * 0.38
  head_y <- y + s * 0.42
  
  tx <- c(x - s * 0.62, x + s * 0.62, x + s * 0.40, x - s * 0.40)
  ty <- c(y - s * 0.50, y - s * 0.50, y + s * 0.15, y + s * 0.15)
  grid.polygon(tx, ty, gp = gpar(fill = torso_col, col = "#0F172A", lwd = 1.2))
  
  if (!is.null(collar_col)) {
    cx <- c(x - s * 0.20, x, x + s * 0.20)
    cy <- c(y + s * 0.15, y - s * 0.10, y + s * 0.15)
    grid.polygon(cx, cy, gp = gpar(fill = collar_col, col = NA))
  }
  
  if (!is.null(tie_col)) {
    tie_x <- c(x, x + s * 0.08, x, x - s * 0.08)
    tie_y <- c(y + s * 0.10, y - s * 0.15, y - s * 0.42, y - s * 0.15)
    grid.polygon(tie_x, tie_y, gp = gpar(fill = tie_col, col = "#7F1D1D", lwd = 0.7))
  }
  
  grid.circle(x, head_y, r = head_r, 
              gp = gpar(fill = head_col, col = "#0F172A", lwd = 1.2))
}

grid.newpage()

}
```

- We have analyzed how electoral outcomes (voters' choices) affect government

- Treating voters' choices as "given" and focusing on what comes later 

- Today: "rules" of elections affect voters' choices and electoral outcomes

---

## Electoral Systems

> An [electoral system]{.alert} is a set of laws and regulations that govern the electoral competition between candidates and parties (Cox 1997)

Including:

- [Electoral formula]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ how votes are translated into seats
- [Ballot structure]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ vote for candidates or parties, how many votes
- [District magnitude]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ how many seats are elected in a district

:::{.fragment}
$\implies$ These procedures change the [decision problem]{.alert} of voters and the [strategies]{.alert} of voters and candidates (e.g., who runs where)
:::


## Our Plan for Today

The key classification of ES based on the electoral formula

- [Majoritarian]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ who receives most votes wins

- [Proportional]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ seats are proportional to votes

- [Mixed]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ some seats allocated through MAJ, some through PROP

:::{.fragment}
:::{.nonincremental}
For each of these families we will see:

- Most popular systems in the world
- The implications for the strategies of voters 
  - Next week we will look at the strategies of parties
- The trade-offs for democratic outcomes
:::
:::


# Majoritarian Electoral Systems {.section}

## Single-Member District Plurality System

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4.0
#| out-width: "600px"
#| out-height: "360px"

grid.newpage()

grid.roundrect(0.50, 0.48, width = 0.96, height = 0.90, r = unit(0.03, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#FAFAFA", col = "#CBD5E1", lwd = 1.5))
grid.text("District Size = 1 (1 Seat)", 0.50, 0.87,
          gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold", col = "#0F172A"))

xs <- c(0.18, 0.40, 0.62, 0.82)
cols <- c("#2563EB", "#DC2626", "#F59E0B", "#16A34A")
bg_cols <- c("#EFF6FF", "#FEF2F2", "#FFFBEB", "#F0FDF4")
shares <- c(0.40, 0.30, 0.20, 0.10)
labels <- c("40%", "30%", "20%", "10%")
n_voters <- c(4, 3, 2, 1)

grid.roundrect(xs[1], 0.75, width = 0.16, height = 0.10, r = unit(0.02, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#DBEAFE", col = "#2563EB", lwd = 2))
grid.text("Elected", xs[1], 0.75, gp = gpar(fontsize = 10.5, fontface = "bold", col = "#1E40AF"))

arr_up <- arrow(angle = 24, length = unit(0.14, "inches"), ends = "last", type = "closed")
grid.lines(c(xs[1], xs[1]), c(0.55, 0.69), arrow = arr_up,
           gp = gpar(col = "#2563EB", fill = "#2563EB", lwd = 4))

for (i in 1:4) {
  draw_person(xs[i], 0.46, s = 0.095, torso_col = cols[i])
  
  bar_h <- shares[i] * 0.44
  bar_y <- 0.10 + bar_h / 2
  grid.roundrect(xs[i], bar_y, width = 0.15, height = bar_h, r = unit(0.015, "snpc"),
                 gp = gpar(fill = bg_cols[i], col = cols[i], lwd = 1.8))
  grid.text(labels[i], xs[i], 0.10 + bar_h + 0.04,
            gp = gpar(fontsize = 11, fontface = "bold", col = cols[i]))
  
  nv <- n_voters[i]
  vx <- seq(xs[i] - 0.022 * (nv - 1) / 2, xs[i] + 0.022 * (nv - 1) / 2, length.out = nv)
  for (v in seq_len(nv)) {
    draw_person(vx[v], 0.13, s = 0.035, torso_col = cols[i], collar_col = NULL)
  }
}
```

::::

- A single vote for a candidate in a single-member district
- The candidate with most votes (plurality) is elected $\rightarrow$ "First-past-the-post" 
- What do you think are the benefits and/or problems of such a system?

## Single-Member District Plurality System

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
**Advantages**

- [Simplicity]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ straightforward for voters to understand where their vote goes
    - The importance of simplicity should not be underestimated
    - Clear rules make clear choices

- One representative per district $\implies$ stronger [accountability]{.alert}
    - Easy to attribute responsibilities
    - Representatives work for their voters

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}

**Criticisms**

- Low district-level [representation]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ only the "largest minority" has its candidate elected
    - E.g., only the largest ethnic group in the district is represented

- Low national-level representation $\rightarrow$ a minority party voted in *every* district can win 0 seats
    - Favor large parties at the expense of small parties with dispersed voters
:::
::::

## Strategic Voting

SMDP encourages [strategic voting]{.alert}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 3.4
#| out-width: "760px"
#| out-height: "300px"

grid.newpage()

draw_person(0.09, 0.38, s = 0.13, torso_col = "#475569", tie_col = "#F59E0B")
grid.text("Voter", 0.09, 0.24, gp = gpar(fontsize = 11.5, fontface = "bold", col = "#0F172A"))

grid.circle(0.145, 0.56, r = 0.012, gp = gpar(fill = "#FFFFFF", col = "#94A3B8", lwd = 1.5))
grid.circle(0.175, 0.61, r = 0.018, gp = gpar(fill = "#FFFFFF", col = "#94A3B8", lwd = 1.5))

pref_x <- 0.34; pref_y <- 0.52; pref_w <- 0.28; pref_h <- 0.72
grid.roundrect(pref_x, pref_y, width = pref_w, height = pref_h, r = unit(0.03, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#FFFFFF", col = "#64748B", lwd = 2))
grid.text("Preferences", pref_x, 0.81, gp = gpar(fontsize = 11.5, fontface = "bold", col = "#0F172A"))

py <- c(0.65, 0.47, 0.29)
p_labels <- c("1. Liberal Democrat", "2. Labour", "3. Conservative")
p_cols <- c("#D97706", "#DC2626", "#2563EB")
p_bgs <- c("#FFFBEB", "#FEF2F2", "#EFF6FF")

for (i in 1:3) {
  grid.roundrect(pref_x, py[i], width = 0.24, height = 0.12, r = unit(0.02, "snpc"),
                 gp = gpar(fill = p_bgs[i], col = p_cols[i], lwd = 1.8))
  grid.text(p_labels[i], pref_x, py[i], gp = gpar(fontsize = 10.5, fontface = "bold", col = p_cols[i]))
}

exp_x <- 0.77; exp_y <- 0.52; exp_w <- 0.36; exp_h <- 0.72
grid.roundrect(exp_x, exp_y, width = exp_w, height = exp_h, r = unit(0.03, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#FAFAFA", col = "#CBD5E1", lwd = 1.8))
grid.text("Expected Votes", exp_x, 0.81, gp = gpar(fontsize = 11.5, fontface = "bold", col = "#0F172A"))

shares <- c(0.14, 0.42, 0.44)
s_text <- c("14%", "42%", "44%")
for (i in 1:3) {
  bar_w <- shares[i] * 0.48
  bar_left <- 0.63
  grid.roundrect(bar_left + bar_w / 2, py[i], width = bar_w, height = 0.10, r = unit(0.015, "snpc"),
                 gp = gpar(fill = p_cols[i], col = "#0F172A", lwd = 1.2))
  grid.text(s_text[i], bar_left + bar_w + 0.02, py[i], just = "left",
            gp = gpar(fontsize = 10.5, fontface = "bold", col = p_cols[i]))
}

grid.lines(c(0.49, 0.61), c(py[1], py[1]),
           gp = gpar(col = "#94A3B8", lwd = 2.5, lty = "dashed"))
grid.text("✕", 0.55, py[1], gp = gpar(fontsize = 16, fontface = "bold", col = "#DC2626"))

arr_vote <- arrow(angle = 24, length = unit(0.15, "inches"), ends = "last", type = "closed")
grid.lines(c(0.49, 0.61), c(py[2], py[2]), arrow = arr_vote,
           gp = gpar(col = "#16A34A", fill = "#16A34A", lwd = 4.5))
grid.text("Vote", 0.55, py[2] + 0.06,
          gp = gpar(fontsize = 10.5, fontface = "bold", col = "#15803D"))
```

- A vote for a candidate with no chances of a plurality is "wasted"
- You may want vote for the "best" candidate **who has chances of winning**
- In SMDP, strategic voting can be more salient than sincere voting

## Single Nontransferable Vote

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
**Advantages**

- More [proportionality]{.alert} relative to SMDP

- Minorities can have their representatives elected even if they are not a plurality

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
**Criticisms**

- More factionalism $\rightarrow$ intraparty competition too

- Personalistic competition + smaller groups of voters needed for election $\implies$ targeted [vote-buying]{.alert} instead of [programmatic]{.alert} appeals

- Less votes to win $\implies$ less need to moderate, more [extremism]{.alert}

:::
::::


## Alternative Vote

Several names: Alternative vote, Instant-runoff vote, Ranked-choice vote


```{r}

}

grid.text("50%", 0.935, y_50 + 0.03, gp = gpar(fontsize = 8.5, fontface = "bold", col = "#64748B"))

cx2 <- c(0.79, 0.885)
bh_b <- 0.46 * 0.48

               gp = gpar(fill = "#FEF2F2", col = "#DC2626", lwd = 1.8))

               gp = gpar(fill = "#FDE68A", col = "#D97706", lwd = 1.8))

           gp = gpar(col = "#DC2626", fill = "#DC2626", lwd = 3.5))

               gp = gpar(fill = "#FEE2E2", col = "#DC2626", lwd = 2))
grid.text("Elected", cx2[2], 0.72, gp = gpar(fontsize = 9.5, fontface = "bold", col = "#991B1B"))
```


- Voters rank candidates by preference
- The candidate with less first preferences is eliminated
- The second preferences of his voters are assigned to the others



## Alternative Vote

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}

**Advantages**

- Advantages of SMDP for [accountability]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ one representative per district

- Voters use their full [preferences]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ less incentives for strategic voting

- Candidates need to rank high for many people $\rightarrow$ broader appeals + between-party bargaining

- The winner is supported by a majority

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}

**Criticisms**

- [Complex]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ voter error is more likely

- Burdensome for voters $\rightarrow$ ranking candidates requires a lot of information

- Relative position in the rankings (not just general "popularity") matters

:::
::::

## Majority-Runoff Two-Round System

Very common for electing presidents

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="70%"}

:::

![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/c/c3/Flag_of_France.svg/1280px-Flag_of_France.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail){width=20%}

![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/0/05/Flag_of_Brazil.svg/1280px-Flag_of_Brazil.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail){width=20%}

![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Flag_of_Chile.svg/1280px-Flag_of_Chile.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail){width=20%}
:::
::::

- If a candidate gets a majority in the first round, he/she wins
- If not, the two most voted candidates go to the second round


## Majority-Runoff Two-Round System

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}

**Advantages**

- Voters have more opportunities to influence the outcome 
  - E.g., vote sincerely in the first round and strategically in the second

- Voters can change their minds between rounds 

- In the second round candidates need to attract others' voters $\rightarrow$ bargaining and [compromise]{.alert}

- The winner is supported by a majority

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}

**Criticisms**

- [Costly]{.alert} for the electoral administration and for voters
  - $\Downarrow$ turnout in the second round

- Very [disproportional]{.alert}

:::
::::




# Proportional Electoral Systems {.section}

## Proportional Systems: General Characteristics

[Proportional]{.alert} systems aim to ensure proportionality between votes and seats

- They favor broad representation of social groups and interests
 
- Typically advocated for multiethnic societies where minority exclusion can threaten peace

- **Main criticisms**: [fragmentation]{.alert}, [instability]{.alert}, and [accountability]{.alert}
  - PR reproduces social divisions without clear incentives to cooperation
  - Coalition govts are more unstable and responsibilities are diluted
  - More chances for fringe or extremist parties


## List PR Systems

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8.8
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| out-width: "800px"
#| out-height: "330px"

grid.newpage()

# Left: Party Lists & Vote Shares
grid.roundrect(0.29, 0.50, width = 0.52, height = 0.90, r = unit(0.03, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#FAFAFA", col = "#CBD5E1", lwd = 1.5))
grid.text("Party Lists", 0.29, 0.89,
          gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold", col = "#0F172A"))

px <- c(0.13, 0.29, 0.45)
pnames <- c("Party A", "Party B", "Party C")
pcols <- c("#2563EB", "#DC2626", "#16A34A")
pbgs <- c("#EFF6FF", "#FEF2F2", "#F0FDF4")
pshares <- c("50%", "30%", "20%")
n_won <- c(5, 3, 2)

for (i in 1:3) {
  grid.roundrect(px[i], 0.47, width = 0.14, height = 0.68, r = unit(0.02, "snpc"),
                 gp = gpar(fill = "#FFFFFF", col = pcols[i], lwd = 2))
  grid.roundrect(px[i], 0.75, width = 0.125, height = 0.08, r = unit(0.015, "snpc"),
                 gp = gpar(fill = pbgs[i], col = NA))
  grid.text(pnames[i], px[i], 0.75, gp = gpar(fontsize = 10, fontface = "bold", col = pcols[i]))
  
  cy <- seq(0.64, 0.24, length.out = 5)
  for (k in 1:5) {
    elected <- k <= n_won[i]
    if (elected) {
      grid.roundrect(px[i], cy[k], width = 0.115, height = 0.075, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
                     gp = gpar(fill = pbgs[i], col = pcols[i], lwd = 1.4))
    }
    grid.text(paste0(k, "."), px[i] - 0.038, cy[k],
              gp = gpar(fontsize = 8.5, fontface = "bold", col = if (elected) pcols[i] else "#94A3B8"))
    draw_person(px[i] + 0.012, cy[k] - 0.005, s = 0.042,
                torso_col = if (elected) pcols[i] else "#CBD5E1", collar_col = NULL)
  }
  
  grid.text(pshares[i], px[i], 0.09, gp = gpar(fontsize = 10.5, fontface = "bold", col = pcols[i]))
}

arr <- arrow(angle = 24, length = unit(0.15, "inches"), ends = "last", type = "closed")
grid.lines(c(0.57, 0.66), c(0.50, 0.50), arrow = arr,
           gp = gpar(col = "#334155", fill = "#334155", lwd = 4))

# Right: Allocated Seats (10 Seats)
grid.roundrect(0.83, 0.50, width = 0.28, height = 0.90, r = unit(0.03, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#FAFAFA", col = "#CBD5E1", lwd = 1.5))
grid.text("Seats (10)", 0.83, 0.89,
          gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold", col = "#0F172A"))

seat_cols <- c(rep("#2563EB", 5), rep("#DC2626", 3), rep("#16A34A", 2))
seat_bgs <- c(rep("#EFF6FF", 5), rep("#FEF2F2", 3), rep("#F0FDF4", 2))
sx_grid <- rep(c(0.77, 0.89), each = 5)
sy_grid <- rep(seq(0.72, 0.22, length.out = 5), 2)

for (s in 1:10) {
  grid.roundrect(sx_grid[s], sy_grid[s], width = 0.09, height = 0.08, r = unit(0.015, "snpc"),
                 gp = gpar(fill = seat_bgs[s], col = seat_cols[s], lwd = 1.8))
  draw_person(sx_grid[s], sy_grid[s] - 0.005, s = 0.048, torso_col = seat_cols[s], collar_col = NULL)
}
```

- Parties present lists of candidates in multimember districts
- Seats are given in proportion to the votes going to the list
- Differences in the "details" of the system are key

## District Magnitude

[District magnitude]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ n. of candidates elected in a district

- The most important factor influencing the proportionality of a system

- Extreme case: a unique list for the whole country 
  - E.g., European Parliament elections in many countries, Netherlands, Israel

- The larger the magnitude, the less direct the link between voters and representatives

## Important Concepts: Electoral Thresholds

[Electoral threshold]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ minimum % of voters a party needs to enter the parliament

- A *natural* threshold is implicit $\rightarrow$ n. of seats is small so there will always be excluded parties

- *Formal* thresholds are used to reduce party fragmentation

- Large thresholds decrease representation and re-introduce strategic voting


## Important Concepts: Type of List

[Types of party lists]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ determine which candidates from the list are elected


::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
**Closed List**

- *Who* is elected depends on the position in the list
- If a party wins $n$ seats, they go to the first $n$ candidates
- Gives [parties]{.alert} full control over [candidates]{.alert}
  - Less personalistic system
  - Can introduce quotas or minority candidates

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
![South African Closed List ballot paper (1994) (Source: Minnekon - Wikimedia Commons)](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/South_African_1994_election_ballot_paper.jpg/960px-South_African_1994_election_ballot_paper.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=thumbnail&_=20221213175716)
:::
::::



## List PR Systems

[Types of party lists]{.alert} $\rightarrow$ determine which candidates from the list are elected


::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
**Open List**

- Voters vote for the list **and** for candidates within the list
- Seats won by the list are allocated based on the number of personal votes instead of list order 
  - More choice to voters, but at the cost of more complexity
  - Re-introduce personal vote
:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
![Danish Open List ballot paper (2019) (Source: Minnekon - Wikimedia Commons)](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Ballot_paper_of_2019_Danish_parliament_election.jpg/960px-Ballot_paper_of_2019_Danish_parliament_election.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=thumbnail&_=20221216121450)
:::
::::



## Single Transferable Vote

The only PR system without lists

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8.8
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| out-width: "820px"
#| out-height: "330px"

grid.newpage()

# Panel 1: Ranked Ballot
grid.roundrect(0.17, 0.50, width = 0.28, height = 0.86, r = unit(0.03, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#FFFFFF", col = "#64748B", lwd = 1.8))

b_bgs <- c("#EFF6FF", "#FEF2F2", "#FFFBEB", "#F0FDF4")
b_ranks <- c("1", "2", "3", "4")
b_names <- c("Candidate A", "Candidate B", "Candidate C", "Candidate D")
for (i in 1:4) {
  grid.roundrect(0.17, by[i], width = 0.23, height = 0.10, r = unit(0.015, "snpc"),
                 gp = gpar(fill = b_bgs[i], col = b_cols[i], lwd = 1.5))

            gp = gpar(fill = "#FFFFFF", col = b_cols[i], lwd = 1.4))

  grid.text(b_names[i], 0.19, by[i], gp = gpar(fontsize = 9, fontface = "bold", col = b_cols[i]))
}

# Right Panel: Multi-Member District (3 Seats)
grid.roundrect(0.66, 0.50, width = 0.62, height = 0.86, r = unit(0.03, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#FAFAFA", col = "#CBD5E1", lwd = 1.5))
grid.text("District Size = 3 (3 Seats)", 0.66, 0.85,
          gp = gpar(fontsize = 11.5, fontface = "bold", col = "#0F172A"))

y_quota <- 0.16 + 0.32 * 0.48
grid.lines(c(0.38, 0.94), c(y_quota, y_quota), gp = gpar(col = "#64748B", lwd = 1.8, lty = "dashed"))
grid.text("Quota", 0.90, y_quota + 0.035, gp = gpar(fontsize = 9, fontface = "bold", col = "#475569"))

cx <- c(0.46, 0.59, 0.72, 0.85)
cols <- c("#2563EB", "#DC2626", "#F59E0B", "#16A34A")
bgs <- c("#EFF6FF", "#FEF2F2", "#FFFBEB", "#F0FDF4")

bh_quota <- 0.32 * 0.48
bh_surp <- 0.12 * 0.48
grid.roundrect(cx[1], 0.16 + bh_quota / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_quota, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = bgs[1], col = cols[1], lwd = 1.8))
grid.roundrect(cx[1], 0.16 + bh_quota + bh_surp / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_surp, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#DBEAFE", col = cols[1], lwd = 1.5, lty = "dotted"))

bh_2 <- 0.34 * 0.48
grid.roundrect(cx[2], 0.16 + bh_2 / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_2, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = bgs[2], col = cols[2], lwd = 1.8))

bh_3_base <- 0.20 * 0.48
bh_3_tr <- 0.14 * 0.48
grid.roundrect(cx[3], 0.16 + bh_3_base / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_3_base, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = bgs[3], col = cols[3], lwd = 1.8))
grid.roundrect(cx[3], 0.16 + bh_3_base + bh_3_tr / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_3_tr, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#FDE68A", col = "#D97706", lwd = 1.8))

bh_4 <- 0.15 * 0.48
grid.roundrect(cx[4], 0.16 + bh_4 / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_4, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = bgs[4], col = cols[4], lwd = 1.5))
grid.text("✕", cx[4], 0.16 + bh_4 / 2, gp = gpar(fontsize = 11, fontface = "bold", col = "#DC2626"))

arr_tr <- arrow(angle = 20, length = unit(0.10, "inches"), ends = "last", type = "closed")
grid.curve(cx[1] + 0.03, 0.16 + bh_quota + bh_surp / 2, cx[3] - 0.03, 0.16 + bh_3_base + bh_3_tr / 2,
           curvature = -0.25, arrow = arr_tr, gp = gpar(col = "#2563EB", fill = "#2563EB", lwd = 2))
grid.curve(cx[4] - 0.02, 0.16 + bh_4, cx[3] + 0.03, 0.16 + bh_3_base + bh_3_tr / 2,
           curvature = 0.30, arrow = arr_tr, gp = gpar(col = "#16A34A", fill = "#16A34A", lwd = 2))

arr_win <- arrow(angle = 24, length = unit(0.12, "inches"), ends = "last", type = "closed")
for (i in 1:3) {
  grid.lines(c(cx[i], cx[i]), c(0.45, 0.64), arrow = arr_win,
             gp = gpar(col = cols[i], fill = cols[i], lwd = 3.5))
  grid.roundrect(cx[i], 0.71, width = 0.105, height = 0.08, r = unit(0.015, "snpc"),
                 gp = gpar(fill = bgs[i], col = cols[i], lwd = 2))
  grid.text(paste0("Seat ", i), cx[i], 0.71, gp = gpar(fontsize = 9.5, fontface = "bold", col = cols[i]))
}
```

:::{.nonincremental}
- $\approx$ to AV in multimember districts
- Voters rank all candidates
- Candidates over a certain **quota** of votes are elected
:::


## Single Transferable Vote

The only PR system without lists

```{r}
#| echo: false

# Panel 1: Ranked Ballot

               gp = gpar(fill = "#FFFFFF", col = "#64748B", lwd = 1.8))
grid.text("Ranked Ballot", 0.17, 0.85, gp = gpar(fontsize = 11.5, fontface = "bold", col = "#0F172A"))

by <- c(0.69, 0.54, 0.39, 0.24)
b_cols <- c("#2563EB", "#DC2626", "#F59E0B", "#16A34A")
b_bgs <- c("#EFF6FF", "#FEF2F2", "#FFFBEB", "#F0FDF4")
b_ranks <- c("1", "2", "3", "4")
b_names <- c("Candidate A", "Candidate B", "Candidate C", "Candidate D")
for (i in 1:4) {
  grid.roundrect(0.17, by[i], width = 0.23, height = 0.10, r = unit(0.015, "snpc"),
                 gp = gpar(fill = b_bgs[i], col = b_cols[i], lwd = 1.5))
  grid.rect(0.085, by[i], width = 0.036, height = 0.06,
            gp = gpar(fill = "#FFFFFF", col = b_cols[i], lwd = 1.4))
  grid.text(b_ranks[i], 0.085, by[i], gp = gpar(fontsize = 9.5, fontface = "bold", col = b_cols[i]))
  grid.text(b_names[i], 0.19, by[i], gp = gpar(fontsize = 9, fontface = "bold", col = b_cols[i]))
}

# Right Panel: Multi-Member District (3 Seats)
grid.roundrect(0.66, 0.50, width = 0.62, height = 0.86, r = unit(0.03, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#FAFAFA", col = "#CBD5E1", lwd = 1.5))
grid.text("District Size = 3 (3 Seats)", 0.66, 0.85,
          gp = gpar(fontsize = 11.5, fontface = "bold", col = "#0F172A"))

y_quota <- 0.16 + 0.32 * 0.48
grid.lines(c(0.38, 0.94), c(y_quota, y_quota), gp = gpar(col = "#64748B", lwd = 1.8, lty = "dashed"))
grid.text("Quota", 0.90, y_quota + 0.035, gp = gpar(fontsize = 9, fontface = "bold", col = "#475569"))

cx <- c(0.46, 0.59, 0.72, 0.85)
cols <- c("#2563EB", "#DC2626", "#F59E0B", "#16A34A")
bgs <- c("#EFF6FF", "#FEF2F2", "#FFFBEB", "#F0FDF4")

bh_quota <- 0.32 * 0.48
bh_surp <- 0.12 * 0.48
grid.roundrect(cx[1], 0.16 + bh_quota / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_quota, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = bgs[1], col = cols[1], lwd = 1.8))
grid.roundrect(cx[1], 0.16 + bh_quota + bh_surp / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_surp, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#DBEAFE", col = cols[1], lwd = 1.5, lty = "dotted"))

bh_2 <- 0.34 * 0.48
grid.roundrect(cx[2], 0.16 + bh_2 / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_2, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = bgs[2], col = cols[2], lwd = 1.8))

bh_3_base <- 0.20 * 0.48
bh_3_tr <- 0.14 * 0.48
grid.roundrect(cx[3], 0.16 + bh_3_base / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_3_base, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = bgs[3], col = cols[3], lwd = 1.8))
grid.roundrect(cx[3], 0.16 + bh_3_base + bh_3_tr / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_3_tr, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = "#FDE68A", col = "#D97706", lwd = 1.8))

bh_4 <- 0.15 * 0.48
grid.roundrect(cx[4], 0.16 + bh_4 / 2, width = 0.08, height = bh_4, r = unit(0.01, "snpc"),
               gp = gpar(fill = bgs[4], col = cols[4], lwd = 1.5))
grid.text("✕", cx[4], 0.16 + bh_4 / 2, gp = gpar(fontsize = 11, fontface = "bold", col = "#DC2626"))

arr_tr <- arrow(angle = 20, length = unit(0.10, "inches"), ends = "last", type = "closed")
grid.curve(cx[1] + 0.03, 0.16 + bh_quota + bh_surp / 2, cx[3] - 0.03, 0.16 + bh_3_base + bh_3_tr / 2,
           curvature = -0.25, arrow = arr_tr, gp = gpar(col = "#2563EB", fill = "#2563EB", lwd = 2))
grid.curve(cx[4] - 0.02, 0.16 + bh_4, cx[3] + 0.03, 0.16 + bh_3_base + bh_3_tr / 2,
           curvature = 0.30, arrow = arr_tr, gp = gpar(col = "#16A34A", fill = "#16A34A", lwd = 2))

arr_win <- arrow(angle = 24, length = unit(0.12, "inches"), ends = "last", type = "closed")
for (i in 1:3) {
  grid.lines(c(cx[i], cx[i]), c(0.45, 0.64), arrow = arr_win,
             gp = gpar(col = cols[i], fill = cols[i], lwd = 3.5))
  grid.roundrect(cx[i], 0.71, width = 0.105, height = 0.08, r = unit(0.015, "snpc"),
                 gp = gpar(fill = bgs[i], col = cols[i], lwd = 2))
  grid.text(paste0("Seat ", i), cx[i], 0.71, gp = gpar(fontsize = 9.5, fontface = "bold", col = cols[i]))
}
```

:::{.nonincremental}
- At each step: least voted candidate is eliminated
- Votes for eliminated candidates **and** surplus votes for elected candidates are assigned to other candidates based on ranked choices
:::



## Single Transferable Vote

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}

**Advantages**

- Maintains the advantages of the AV in terms of voter choice while being proportional

- More control over candidate choice than list PR

- Typically allows cross-party voting $\rightarrow$ not the case in most list PR

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}

**Criticisms**

- All criticisms of candidate-centered systems
  - Personalism, intraparty factionalism

- $\Uparrow$ n. of candidates to be ranked
  - Even more difficult for voters to make an informed choice
  - Lower district magnitude mitigates the problem but reduces proportionality too 

:::
::::


# Mixed Electoral Systems {.section}

## Mixed Electoral Systems

Shares of voters elected under majoritarian and proportional systems

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
- Voters have two votes 
- Typically multiple electoral [tiers]{.alert}
  - Majoritarian seats in low-level districts with small magnitude
  - Proportional seats in high-level constituency (regional or national)
:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
![New Zealand ballot paper (1993 -- sample)](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/da/New_Zealand_MMP_voting_paper.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled&_=20110327014732)
:::
::::

## Mixed Electoral Systems
::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}

**Advantages**

- Combine the appealing features of the two systems

- PROP $\implies$ proportional outcomes and [social]{.alert} representation

- MAJ $\implies$ [territorial]{.alert} representation and direct accountability

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}

**Criticisms**

- Two different classes of legislators with different "loyalties" $\rightarrow$ parties and voters

- Low cohesion

- May be difficult for voters to understand the aggregation of votes

:::
::::


# Summing Up {.section}


## What We Learned

- Electoral systems are "the rules of the game" of how political power is distributed

- Different rules imply different [choices]{.alert} and [strategies]{.alert} for voters

- Choosing an ES implies trade-offs

- [Majoritarian]{.alert} systems favor clear majorities and responsibilities
  - But less representation for some social groups

- [Proportional]{.alert} systems favor broad representation 
  - But more fragmented and potentially unstable governments


## Important Takeaways

- Voters always weigh sincere and strategic voting considerations

- The electoral system makes one or the other more relevant

- This has a **key implication** for the study of politics: 
$\implies$ we generally cannot make inferences about what voters would do under an ES from their behavior under another ES

- E.g., "If the UK adopted list PR, Labour would win voters in these areas"
  - Maybe yes, but a lot of voters would change their vote
  - Knowing this, new parties would have an incentive to emerge
  - So everything would change

- Next week: we will see that the number of parties also depends on the ES
